- Overestimate prices in the short term after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (sentiment > 0.3).  
- Underestimate prices after strong downward moves or negative sentiment (sentiment < 0.1), particularly in the first 10 days of the forecast horizon.  
- Model tends to overshoot early in the forecast (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is high; apply a 5–10% downward adjustment to early forecast values.  
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is > 10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 5–8% unless sentiment is strongly bullish.  
- When sentiment is consistently low or negative, model overcorrects downward; increase forecast by 2–5% to avoid underestimating rebound.  
- Forecast horizon 10–15 days: model often misses downward corrections; add a 3–5% buffer for downward momentum if sentiment is weak.  
- Avoid overconfidence in 30-day forecasts when sentiment is volatile; reduce forecast variance by 15–20% if sentiment swings > 0.2 in last 5 days.
